full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short is that the suit land originally belonged to Abdul Gafur under land lord Upendra Chandra Basu and the C. S. record was prepared in his name correctly. That before few years of C. S. operation Abdul Gafur kept the suit property mortgaged with Bakshu Sheikh alias Bepari by registered mortgage deed accepting Tk. 250/- from him and handed over possession of the suit land to Bakshu Sheikh @ Bepari; that it was settled that the suit land would be returned by execution of a registered deed if the money is returned. In the C. S. khatian it was recorded that Bakshu Sheikh alias Bepari is in possession of the suit property through cot kabala. That subsequently Mir Abdul Gafur converted that Kot kabala into Sub-kabala by accepting another Tk. 150/-and gave up the claim of the suit land. Bakshu Shiekh possessed the suit land for more than twelve years and after his death his heirs have become the owners of the suit land. That the present plaintiffs are successive heirs of Bakhsu Sheikh @ Bepari. That in the month of Chaitra, 1400 B.S. when the plaintiffs went to pay rent of the suit land in the local Tahsil Office they came to know that the S. A. record of the suit land had been prepared in the name of the defendants and hence the suit. 

 5. Both the parties adduced some witnesses before the trial Court in order to prove their respective cases. The trial Court, on consideration of those evidence, dismissed the suit making observations to the effect that the S. A. khatian of the suit land was prepared in the name of the defendants 40 years before, but during this long period the plaintiffs did not take any step to correct the S. A. khatian of the suit land and to pay rent of the suit land and that these facts falsify plaintiffs' case that their predecessor got the suit land from Abdul Gafur and prove the defendants case that Abdul Gafur sold the suit land orally to the predecessors of the defendants. The appellate Court below reversed these findings and decisions of the trial Court on making observations to the effect that according the entry of the C. S. record the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs namely Bakshu Sheikh alias Bepari used to possess the suit land on the strength of 'cot kabala' and that this entry of the C. S. record of rights can not be presumed to be false in the absence of any evidence at all, that in this suit the onus was on the defendants to prove that Abdul Gafur released the suit property from Bakshu Sheikh alias Bepari upon payment of debt, but no such evidence could be adduced by the defendants. The appellate Court below has made observations to the effect also that the defendants have failed to adduce any evidence whatsoever to prove their case that Abdul Gafur sold the suit land orally to their predecessors in the year 1340 B.S.
